entry_conditions: Accept demonstrated incoming acquisition and transport states across the full expanded slices, not just completed grasps. The measured starts have about 0.08 m total finger opening and TCP heights spanning approximately 0.044-0.135 m. Use two causal observations of qpos 0:9, qvel 9:18, TCP pose 18:25, red pose 25:32, blue pose 32:39, red goal 41:44 and blue goal 44:47. Positions and goals are world metres; rotations are wxyz. Joint/finger motion, TCP-to-object offset, object motion and height distinguish open descent, partial grasp, lift, carry and lowering. No elapsed trajectory index or externally supplied grasp flag is required. Nominated red/blue role IDs are inferred from proximity and observed protection support, not future labels. In blue acquisition/carry, preserve red if live containment and observed opening or separation support prior release. Negative airborne height margins around object z=0.28 m are expected and must not be interpreted as a demand for immediate descent.
exit_conditions: For each live object, rotate all eight cube corners with half extent 0.02 m. XY margins are 0.06 minus the largest absolute corner offset from its own goal in each axis; the height margin is 0.011 minus absolute centre-height error about goal z=0.02 m. An object is at_goal iff all three margins are nonnegative. One observed conjunction red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal completes the task; no opening, clearance, velocity limit or sustained hold is required. demo10000/690 supports completion with blue z=0.02284 m and a -1 command. Physical readiness is reported separately: opening fingers, settled object and separating/high TCP are useful transfer cues. The demonstrated final context has both objects near z=0.02 m, fingers near 0.04 m each, TCP near z=0.299 m. The first occurrence instead ends during a high approach toward blue, not with both blocks placed.
overlap_role: The policy imitates every assigned expanded action, including incoming open low approach, closure and lift as well as carry. The shared red outgoing transition includes actual lowering, finger opening, settling, retreat and the high approach to the next object. In demo10000 the acquisition overlaps [80,185) and [470,585), and the red outgoing overlap [265,425), are all retained. Equivalent measured overlaps in the other eleven original demonstrations are also retained without trimming or normalization refitting. Causal pose/finger/motion features allow takeover partway through these transitions. Action-outcome contract regularization is masked to real future placement windows and sufficiently confident causal predictions during training, so the already negative airborne margin alone does not replace acquisition with a descent shortcut. The acquire successor shares the bridge and can finish release/retreat; neither policy relies on a preset switch index.
successor_readiness: Pass current world goals and per-object live contract margins, both recent raw observations, qpos/qvel, TCP/object poses, finger openings, observed motion and the nominated role/protection interpretation. In model.diagnostics, IDs 0/1 denote red/blue and -1 denotes both observed as protected; this nomination is not certified contact or a carried-object sensor. Distinguish contained-but-held/descending from released-but-TCP-low and released-with-TCP-separating. Protection support uses live containment, object displacement below 0.003 m over the history, and either total opening above 0.065 m or TCP separation above 0.08 m. It can protect red while the fingers are closed on blue. The separate readiness proxy uses containment, both fingers above 0.035 m, TCP distance above 0.06 m and TCP above the object by 0.05 m. These readiness/protection thresholds are demonstrated-context proxies, not additions to task success or hard invocation rejection rules. Predicted future probabilities/margins must remain labelled predictions; a successor must use live observations to preserve the completed block while disengaging or approaching the next block.
failure_signatures: Centre-only containment that misses an outlying rotated corner, reported success while centre height exceeds tolerance, red leaving its pad during blue placement, or large out-of-pattern joint targets contradict the contract/prior. A satisfied live contract with a loaded closed gripper is task completion but not necessarily an empty-hand transfer state. A causal event prediction suggesting imminent placement while the live block remains in high transport is a model-calibration warning, not observed progress. Compare new live poses with expected motion before extending an invocation; do not treat a forecast as a sensor. This implementation has no persistent disagreement monitor or online rollout-energy optimizer, and no demonstrated recovery for falls or off-pad disturbance.
continuation_guidance: Continue this learned policy through partial grasp/lift/carry and normal lowering when the desired live contract has not yet been reached. After red containment, continue or transfer within the shared opening/settling/retreat bridge according to observed finger and TCP separation; the full slice also supports continued high approach toward blue. At demo10000/305 red is released with fingers near 0.03976 m but TCP still only z=0.02286 m, whereas /350 is a high retreat and /424 a next-object approach. At /692 blue is opening, /700 is open but low, /720 is retreating and /750 is high. When both live predicates hold, stopping satisfies the given task even before opening. If an empty-hand successor is desired, optional further learned disengagement reaches a more useful state. Invocation duration is chosen from observations, not these source indices. Runtime forward uses only learned epsilon prediction and causal event/readiness conditioning; training-time amortized outcome losses do not introduce a scripted action controller.
limitations: The support consists of successful original demonstrations, not perturbation/recovery trials. Observed separation and finger opening suggest release but do not directly measure contact or load. Future pose and readiness targets are training labels only and are masked at segment boundaries. The exact shared full-demonstration normalizer is used unchanged. There is no IK, physics simulator, image encoder, safety guarantee, action equivariance, online candidate reranking or online gradient guidance. Counterfactual forecast calibration, novel rotations/heights, shifted or moving pads, clutter and falling-block recovery remain untested. The extra diagnostics method is available in the model but is not assumed to be automatically surfaced by the framework; the inference agent can evaluate the documented live geometry itself.
